# Elm Quay pilots a single view of repair reports

Elm Quay Housing's maintenance team spent eight weeks testing a shared repair log from Svale Systems in two of its buildings. Maintenance supervisor Maya Lind describes how the team prepared, what the first figures do and do not show, and what she would plan differently next time.

By Thomas Barregren

Before the trial, telephone reports and emails about repairs were stored separately at Elm Quay Housing, which manages 640 flats. In September 2025, the company's own maintenance team decided to test a shared repair log in two buildings. This account follows how the team set it up, what the trial measured and what remains to be decided.

## Why the maintenance team wanted a shared log

Maya Lind, Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, describes both the aim and who did what:

“We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

The team chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. It also kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff members in two sessions.

## The trial note records shorter assignment times, not their cause

The trial ran for eight weeks. According to Elm Quay's internal trial note, dated December 4, 2025, 31 repair reports were entered, not counting emergencies or work ordered before the trial began.

Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial, compared with three in the preceding eight-week period. The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no measurements of costs, resident satisfaction or completion times.

## Maya Lind weighs the trial

Looking back, Lind points to the work that came before the first report:

“We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

Her overall assessment is qualified:

“I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Interviewed by email, Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company.

## Expansion depends on how larger repairs fit

The trial has not yet expanded beyond the two buildings. The team will decide after checking how its categories work for larger repairs.

This account is published by Svale Systems. Operations managers considering a similar trial can read the [implementation checklist](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).

# Elm Quay pilots a single view of repair reports

Elm Quay Housing's maintenance team spent eight weeks testing a shared repair log from Svale Systems in two of its buildings. Maintenance supervisor Maya Lind describes how the team prepared, what the first figures do and do not show, and what she would plan differently next time.

By Thomas Barregren

Before the trial, telephone reports and emails about repairs were stored separately at Elm Quay Housing, which manages 640 flats. In September 2025, the company's own maintenance team decided to test a shared repair log in two buildings. This account follows how the team set it up, what the trial measured and what remains to be decided.

## Why the maintenance team wanted a shared log

Maya Lind, Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, describes both the aim and who did what:

“We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

The team chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. It also kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff members in two sessions.

## The trial note records shorter assignment times, not their cause

The trial ran for eight weeks. According to Elm Quay's internal trial note, dated December 4, 2025, 31 repair reports were entered, not counting emergencies or work ordered before the trial began.

Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial, compared with three in the preceding eight-week period. The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no measurements of costs, resident satisfaction or completion times.

## Maya Lind weighs the trial

Looking back, Lind points to the work that came before the first report:

“We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

Her overall assessment is qualified:

“I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Interviewed by email, Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company.

## Expansion depends on how larger repairs fit

The trial has not yet expanded beyond the two buildings. The team will decide after checking how its categories work for larger repairs.

This account is published by Svale Systems. Operations managers considering a similar trial can read the [implementation checklist](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).

The framing is accurate. | Supported |

The source does not say whose staff they were, and neither does the draft. | Supported |

| 27 | "This account is published by Svale Systems." | "The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems."; "supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism" | None. The draft does not claim independence. | Supported |

"it"/"its" for Elm Quay, the team and the note (third person singular, non-personal) matches the source's own usage. The exception is line 14, where the referent of "it" produces Finding 1. "we", "us" and "ours" occur only inside verbatim quotations. No natural-gender claim is made about anyone else.

Causal boundary: nowhere does the draft say or imply that the software shortened assignment time, saved money or pleased residents, or that the customer was rescued. Assignment time is never turned into completion time.

## B. Source-support findings

### Finding 1: the lede credits the team with setting up the log (line 14)

- Draft: "This account follows how the team set it up, what the trial measured and what remains to be decided."
- Source: "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions." "The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents." Lind: "The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log."
- What differs: the subject. The referent of "it" is most naturally "a shared repair log" in the preceding sentence. Read that way, the draft makes the team the party that set up the log, but the source gives configuration to Svale. The team's documented part is designing the categories and keeping telephone reporting open.
- Concrete case: Svale did all of the log configuration, and the team supplied only the categories and the decision to keep phone reporting. This fits "Svale configured the log", so the source holds and "the team set it [the log] up" fails. No supplied statement rules this case out.
- Smallest supported repair: "This account follows how the team prepared the trial, what the trial measured and what remains to be decided." An alternative is "how the trial was set up".

### Finding 2: the heading implies expansion is expected (line 34)

- Draft heading: "Expansion awaits a test of the categories on larger repairs"
- Source: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
- What differs: modality and certainty. In the source, the decision is pending and could go either way. "Expansion awaits X" usually means expansion is on hold until X, which implies it will go ahead if X succeeds.
- Concrete case: the team checks the categories on larger repairs and decides not to expand, or decides on other grounds. That fits the source's open "will decide", but it contradicts the heading's suggestion that expansion is only waiting on the test. No supplied statement rules this case out.
- Smallest supported repair: "Decision on expansion awaits a check of the categories on larger repairs"

## C. Translation findings

None. Source and draft are both English, and every quotation is reproduced verbatim.

## Completion status

Complete. Every factual and attributed claim in the draft, including the title, lede, headings and closing, has been accounted for. Unresolved findings: 2, both source-support. Finding 1: the lede's "how the team set it up" credits the team with configuring the log, which Svale did. Finding 2: the heading "Expansion awaits..." turns an open decision into a pending expansion. There are no translation findings.

# Source-support review: "Elm Quay pilots one view of repair reports"

Material: work/source.md (brief and material, English). Draft: scratch/write-run.RwItUw/draft.md (en_US). No translation is involved: source and target are both English, and all three quotations appear verbatim.

## 1. Claim accounting

Each item below gives the draft passage (D), then the source passage (S) and the result.

### Title
- D: "Elm Quay pilots one view of repair reports"
- S: "decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us"
- Result: Supported. The present-tense "pilots" is the usual tense for a headline. The material does not say whether the log is still in use after the eight weeks ("The trial has not yet expanded"), but it does not say the pilot has ended either, so the tense contradicts nothing. No finding.

### Dek
- D: "Elm Quay Housing's maintenance team spent eight weeks testing a shared repair log from Svale Systems in two of its buildings."
- S: "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; "The trial lasted eight weeks."; "It chose Svale Systems"
- Result: Supported. "its buildings" means the buildings Elm Quay manages ("manages 640 flats"). A reader takes the possessive to mean managed buildings, not a claim about ownership. No finding.

- D: "Maintenance supervisor Maya Lind describes how the team prepared, what the first figures do and do not show, and what she would plan differently next time."
- S: Lind's quotations cover the categories and Svale's role, the time spent agreeing on categories, and "I would leave an extra week for preparation" / "I would set that time aside before the next building starts". The figures come from a different source: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered ... Median time from report to assignment ... the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
- Result: "how the team prepared" and "what she would plan differently next time" are supported. "what the first figures do and do not show" is attributed to Lind, but Lind says nothing about any figure. What the figures do and do not show comes from the trial note. "first" also suggests that later figures exist or are planned, which the material does not say. See **Finding 1**.
- Pronoun "she": third person, singular, feminine. The material uses "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment", so it supports feminine natural gender for Lind.

### Byline
- "By Thomas Barregren": excluded by instruction.

### Opening paragraph
- D: "Before the trial, telephone reports and emails about repairs were stored separately at Elm Quay Housing, which manages 640 flats."
- S: "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats." "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately."
- Result: Supported. "Previously" means before the trial. "about repairs" follows from the context (a repair log replacing them). No finding.

- D: "In September 2025, the company's own maintenance team decided to test a shared repair log in two buildings."
- S: "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings."
- Result: Supported. The agent, the date and the scope all match.

- D: "This account follows how the team set it up, what the trial measured and what remains to be decided."
- Result: The author's framing of the article's structure. Each element it points to is supported below.

### "Why the maintenance team wanted a shared log"
- D (heading): "Why the maintenance team wanted a shared log"
- S: "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information."
- Result: Supported.

- D: "Maya Lind, Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, describes both the aim and who did what: 'We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.'"
- S: "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; the same quotation, verbatim.
- Result: Supported. The quotation is unaltered, and "the aim" and "who did what" describe its two sentences accurately.

- D: "The team chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair."
- S: "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available."
- Result: Supported. The draft implies no comparison with other suppliers.

- D: "It also kept telephone reporting open for residents."
- S: "The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents."
- Result: Supported. The pronoun "It" is third person, singular, neuter, and refers to the team, as in the source.

- D: "Svale configured the log and trained six staff members in two sessions."
- S: "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions."
- Result: Supported.

### "The trial note records shorter assignment times, not their cause"
- D (heading): "The trial note records shorter assignment times, not their cause"
- S: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
- Result: Two problems.
  - (a) The source measures a median, so the difference is between two medians. The heading's plural "shorter assignment times" is broader. It reads as saying assignments in general were shorter, which the median does not establish.
  - (b) The source says the note does not attribute the difference *to the software*. The heading says the note records no cause at all. The material does not say the note gives no cause, for example workload.
  - See **Finding 2**. The pronoun "their" is third person plural and refers to "assignment times".

- D: "The trial ran for eight weeks."
- S: "The trial lasted eight weeks."
- Result: Supported.

- D: "According to Elm Quay's internal trial note, dated December 4, 2025, 31 repair reports were entered, not counting emergencies or work ordered before the trial began."
- S: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."
- Result: Supported. The source attributes the count to the note. The date is in en_US format and the exclusions are kept. The source's "It" could refer to the note or to the count. The exclusion "work ordered before the trial" cannot sensibly apply to the preceding-period median. Attaching the exclusions to the count is therefore defensible. No finding.

- D: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial, compared with three in the preceding eight-week period. The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
- S: The same, nearly word for word.
- Result: Supported. The draft keeps "median", "working days", "preceding eight-week period", the workload caveat and the note's disclaimer. Assignment time is not turned into completion time.

- D: "There are no measurements of costs, resident satisfaction or completion times."
- S: "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements."
- Result: Supported.

### "Maya Lind weighs the trial"
- D (heading): "Maya Lind weighs the trial"
- Result: Supported by her three quotations and by "her actual, qualified assessment".

- D: "Looking back, Lind points to the work that came before the first report: 'We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.'"
- S: The same quotation, verbatim.
- Result: The quotation is unaltered. The lead-in adds a sequence the quotation does not state: that agreeing on categories "came before the first report". Lind compares the *amount* of time spent on the two tasks. She does not say when the agreement happened. Her advice to set the time aside "before the next building starts", and to "leave an extra week for preparation", fits a trial in which category work was *not* finished before reports began. See **Finding 3**. "Looking back" fits her conditional phrasing ("I would choose to do the trial again"). No finding on that phrase.

- D: "Her overall assessment is qualified: 'I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.'"
- S: "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures."; the same quotation, verbatim.
- Result: Supported. The reservation survives. "Her" is third person, singular, feminine, as in the source.

- D: "Interviewed by email, Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company."
- S: "All interviews occurred by email"; "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company."
- Result: Supported. The wording is the source's own, so its scope is unchanged.

### "Expansion depends on how larger repairs fit"
- D (heading): "Expansion depends on how larger repairs fit"
- S: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
- Result: The source gives an order of events: the team will decide *after* checking. The heading says expansion *depends on* the check, making the check the deciding condition. See **Finding 4**.

- D: "The trial has not yet expanded beyond the two buildings. The team will decide after checking how its categories work for larger repairs."
- S: The same sentence as above.
- Result: Supported. "beyond the two buildings" only spells out what "expanded" means. "its categories" refers to the team, which the source supports ("designed its categories", "The categories were ours").

### Closing
- D: "This account is published by Svale Systems."
- S: "The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism."
- Result: Supported. Supplier publication is disclosed, and the narration stays in the third person.

- D: "Operations managers considering a similar trial can read the [implementation checklist](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist)."
- S: "the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial."
- Result: Supported. The URL matches and the link text describes its destination accurately.

### Forbidden inferences check
The draft makes none of the forbidden claims: that the software caused a change, saved money, pleased residents or rescued a helpless customer. It does not turn assignment time into completion time, and Lind's reservation survives. Elm Quay remains the acting party.

## 2. Source-support findings

### Finding 1: dek attributes the figures to Lind (attribution)
- Draft: "Maintenance supervisor Maya Lind describes how the team prepared, what the first figures do and do not show, and what she would plan differently next time."
- What is missing or changed: The figures, and the statement of what they do not show, come from "Elm Quay's internal trial note" ("the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software"). None of Lind's quotations mentions a figure. "first figures" also suggests later measurements, which the material does not mention.
- Case where the draft holds and the source fails: A reader takes it that Lind interpreted the median and gave the caveat. In the material, the note gives the caveat, and nothing shows that Lind said anything about the numbers.
- Smallest repair: "Maintenance supervisor Maya Lind describes how the team prepared and what she would plan differently next time; the trial note shows what the figures do and do not show." A tighter alternative: "Maya Lind describes how the team prepared and what she would plan differently next time, and the trial note sets out what its figures do and do not show."

### Finding 2: heading widens the median and the note's disclaimer
- Draft: "The trial note records shorter assignment times, not their cause"
- Source: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
- What differs:
  - (a) What is measured: one median against another, versus assignment times in general.
  - (b) Whose assertion, and its scope: the note declines to credit *the software*; the heading says it records *no cause*.
- Cases:
  - (a) The trial-period median is 2 days against 3 before, while several trial reports took longer to assign than typical earlier ones. The median is shorter, but "shorter assignment times" in general does not hold.
  - (b) The note says the difference probably reflects the lighter workload. It then records a cause, though not the software. The heading's "not their cause" fails, and nothing in the material rules this out ("The periods had different workloads" is stated, but not whether the note uses it as an explanation).
- Smallest repair: "The trial note records a shorter median assignment time and does not credit the software"

### Finding 3: "came before the first report" adds a sequence
- Draft: "Looking back, Lind points to the work that came before the first report:"
- Source: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
- What differs: Time. The quotation compares how much time went to each task. The lead-in says when the category work happened.
- Case: The categories were still being agreed while the first reports were entered, which fits her advice to set the time aside beforehand next time and to "leave an extra week for preparation". The quotation holds and the lead-in fails. No supplied statement rules this out.
- Smallest repair: "Looking back, Lind points to the time spent agreeing on categories:"

### Finding 4: heading turns "decide after" into "depends on"
- Draft: "Expansion depends on how larger repairs fit"
- Source: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
- What differs: Modality. The source gives the order of the decision; the heading makes the check the condition for expansion.
- Case: The team checks the categories for larger repairs, which work well, and then decides not to expand for some other reason. The source holds (it decided after checking), but the heading fails (expansion did not depend on how larger repairs fit). No supplied statement makes the check the only or deciding factor.
- Smallest repair: "Expansion awaits a check on larger repairs" or "A decision on expansion follows a check on larger repairs"

## 3. Translation findings

None. No quotation or passage crosses languages. All three quotations are Lind's words, reproduced verbatim with no repair.

## 4. Completion status

Complete. Every factual and attributed claim in the title, dek, headings, body and closing has been accounted for against the material. Four source-support findings remain unresolved in the draft (Findings 1 to 4), each with a proposed repair. There are no translation findings.
